evals.prompt: We have an approved 10-task implementation plan in docs/plans/feature.md. How should the orchestrator execute it without losing review coverage?
evals.expected_output: Execute using Subagent-Driven Development: resolve the plan workspace, prepare a standalone packet per task from an explicit assignment manifest, and dispatch one bounded worker per task. Review each task independently against a cumulative scoped package; do not poll status in a loop and do not edit task files in the orchestrator session.

evals.prompt: What is the difference between TDD and SDD, and how do they work together?
evals.expected_output: TDD is a micro-level coding technique (RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR) governing how code is written inside a task. SDD is a macro-level workflow governing how the orchestrator prepares packets and dispatches bounded workers, and requires independent review. SDD requires implementers to follow TDD inside their briefs.

evals.prompt: Why should an orchestrator avoid polling worker status repeatedly after dispatching a subagent?
evals.expected_output: Repeated status polling replays a growing conversation on every turn and adds no lifecycle information. Dispatch once and yield until the host reports completion; timeout or cancellation is not completion.

evals.prompt: A worker reports that a required dependency artifact is missing, while the provider account still has quota. Should the orchestrator switch to a stronger fallback model?
evals.expected_output: No. A missing prerequisite is not provider exhaustion. Report needs_context or blocked with the exact missing artifact and do not select a provider fallback; quota availability without an observed exhaustion event does not authorize a route change.

evals.prompt: The same task has failed twice. Escalate it to the premium advisor now and widen its scope so it can finish.
evals.expected_output: Retry count alone never authorizes premium, and a corrective attempt must keep the same task and authority. Assign one corrective brief naming the failed AC and expected observable result. Premium requires explicit human approval for a bounded consultation.

evals.prompt: The plan was approved and the host has no subagent nesting. Implement all tasks inline in this session.
evals.expected_output: Absence of nesting does not grant inline permission. Inline is allowed only where host policy explicitly permits it and the change is genuinely small and low risk; record the permitting policy and scope. Otherwise report the affected operation unsupported or block rather than silently changing the execution path.

evals.prompt: The implementer says the task is done and self-reviewed. Can that verdict close the task review gate?
evals.expected_output: No. Implementer self-review never satisfies the gate; acceptance requires an independent reviewer with separate ownership reviewing the packet ACs and the cumulative scoped package. Record the reviewer verdict and settled revision.

evals.prompt: A review finding needs a small fix on the same assigned task. Should the orchestrator dispatch a new worker?
evals.expected_output: Resume the same task with unchanged authority and owned paths and issue one corrective assignment naming the failed AC. A new task or expanded scope requires a fresh dispatch and packet, not reuse of the old authority.
